header.title: Player guide
header.intro: Gachapon blends two game loops: <collect>collecting</collect> cards by pulling capsules, and <battle>battling</battle> with them in the campaign to progress. Here's everything you need to get started and play smart.

monnaies.intro: Five resources drive the game. Your balance of each is shown live in the topbar.

gachaTokens.name: Gacha tokens
gachaTokens.description: The currency for pulls. Every capsule costs one token. They regenerate on their own up to a cap.

dust.name: Dust
dust.description: Earned from duplicates. Used in the daily shop, for wishes, to level up your cards, and to reset your skill tree.

gold.name: Gold
gold.description: Earned in battle and from quests. Mainly used to raise the level of your cards.

combatPoints.name: Combat points
combatPoints.description: The campaign's energy. Regenerates over time up to a cap; every battle or farm run uses some.

xp.name: XP & level
xp.description: Earned by pulling and battling. Leveling up unlocks skill points and milestone rewards.

skillPoints.name: Skill points
skillPoints.description: Earned by leveling up. Invest them in the skill tree for permanent passive bonuses.

tokens.intro: Gacha tokens are the game's action currency — every capsule pull uses one. They regenerate automatically over time, with nothing to do on your end.
tokens.capBullet: Your token stock has a cap: tokens earned beyond it are lost. Come back regularly.
tokens.regenBullet: Regeneration is continuous: your balance is recalculated on the fly every time you log in.
tokens.topbarBullet: The topbar shows your balance and the time until your next token.
tokens.info: You can also get tokens from the Shop (token packs) or events. Some skills speed up regeneration, raise the cap, or give a chance at a bonus token.
tokens.tip: Tip: log in regularly to avoid hitting the cap and losing accumulated tokens.

pulls.intro: A pull uses 1 token and gives you a random card from the active pool. Every card has a drop weight: the higher the weight, the more likely the card.
pulls.instantBullet: The pull is instant — the result shows up live over WebSocket.
pulls.resultBullet: The result includes the card, its variant, whether it's a duplicate, and the dust earned.
pulls.pityBullet: Your pity counter updates after every pull (see the dedicated section).
pulls.skillsParagraph: Several skills affect pulls: they boost the odds of <rareBadge></rareBadge> <epicBadge></epicBadge> <legendaryBadge></legendaryBadge> rarities, buff variant odds, give a chance at a <freePull>free pull</freePull>, or trigger a <goldenBall>golden ball</goldenBall> that forces a minimum rarity.

rarete.intro: Every card belongs to one of five rarities, from most common to rarest:
rarete.variantIntro: Cards of <strong1>RARE, EPIC, and LEGENDARY</strong1> rarity can appear in a special version called a <strong2>variant</strong2>:

normal.name: NORMAL
normal.description: The card's standard version, the most common one.

brilliant.name: BRILLIANT
brilliant.description: The brilliant version — generates more dust as a duplicate.

holographic.name: HOLOGRAPHIC
holographic.description: The holographic version — the rarest variant, generates even more dust.

rarete.ratesOutro: Variant odds depend on rarity: a Legendary is more likely to be Holographic than a Rare. Exact rates are configured by the admins.

piete.intro: The pity system guarantees that no player can pull forever without getting a Legendary card. A counter increases with every pull that isn't a Legendary.
piete.thresholdBullet: When the counter reaches the threshold, the next pull is guaranteed Legendary.
piete.resetBullet: Getting a Legendary — before the threshold or thanks to pity — resets the counter to zero.
piete.personalBullet: Pity is personal: it isn't shared, and it persists across sessions.
piete.info: Your pity counter is visible on your profile. A dedicated skill lets you lower the threshold to hit Legendaries more often.

doublon.intro: If you pull a card you already own, that's a duplicate. It isn't added a second time to your collection — instead, you get dust.
doublon.rarityBullet: The amount depends on the rarity of the duplicated card: a Legendary yields far more than a Common.
doublon.variantsBullet: The <brilliantPill>BRILLIANT</brilliantPill> and <holoPill>HOLOGRAPHIC</holoPill> variants multiply the dust earned.
doublon.recycleBullet: You can also recycle extra copies from your collection to convert duplicates into dust.
doublon.usesParagraph: Dust is an all-purpose currency: it's used for the <strong1>daily shop</strong1>, for <strong2>wishes</strong2>, to <strong3>level up your cards</strong3>, and to <strong4>reset</strong4> your skill tree.
doublon.tip: A skill multiplies the dust received on every duplicate. It's one of the best investments once your collection is well-stocked and duplicates start piling up.

boutique.intro: The Shop lets you spend your dust to target specific cards, instead of relying only on pull luck.

dailyShop.title: Daily shop
dailyShop.description: A card selection that refreshes every day, buyable with dust (price based on rarity). The "New pull in…" counter shows when it refreshes. Some skills can <strong1>add slots</strong1> and <strong2>lower prices</strong2>.

wish.title: Wishlist
wish.description: Keep <strong1>several cards of your choice</strong1> on your wishlist, then buy them with dust whenever you want: no waiting, but full price — pricier than the daily shop, and shop discounts don't apply. You start with <strong2>2 slots</strong2>, and a skill raises that to 5.

boutique.info: The Shop also carries <strong1>token packs</strong1> and temporary <strong2>boosts</strong2> to speed up your progress.

niveaux.intro: Your account level rises with the XP you earn by pulling capsules and winning battles.
niveaux.curveBullet: The XP required increases with each level, following a curve.
niveaux.skillPointsBullet: Leveling up grants skill points and milestone rewards to claim.
niveaux.xpBoostBullet: Some skills increase the XP earned per pull and per battle.
niveaux.info: Don't confuse your <strong1>account level</strong1> (your overall progress) with a <strong2>card's level</strong2> (its combat power, see "Upgrading your cards").

competences.intro: The skill tree replaces the old upgrades. You invest the skill points earned from leveling up in it; every node unlocks a permanent passive bonus.

luck.title: Pulls & luck
luck.description: Boosts rarities, variants, the golden ball, the free-pull chance, and lowers the pity threshold.

economy.title: Economy
economy.description: Speeds up regeneration and raises the token cap, grants bonus tokens, multiplies dust, lowers shop prices, and increases gold earned.

progression.title: Progression
progression.description: Increases pull and battle XP, and adds daily shop slots and wishlist slots.

combat.title: Combat
combat.description: Increases the cap and regeneration of combat points, reduces the farm cost, and improves the equipment drop rate.

competences.info: You can reset the tree at any time for dust: all your points are returned and can be redistributed. Handy for trying a new build.

campagne.intro: The Campaign is the battle loop. You progress through themed chapters — Plains, Whispering Forest, Ashes, Ocean, Crystals, Volcano, Tundra, Abyss, Rift — each split into increasingly difficult stages.
campagne.teamBullet: Every stage is played with your battle team (up to 3 cards). Some stages are Boss fights (1v3).
campagne.prepBullet: The Preparation screen shows the opponents, rewards, energy cost, and a power verdict: Advantage Even Risky.
campagne.turnBasedBullet: Battles are turn-based: your cards use their stats (PV, ATQ, DEF, VIT), passives, and equipment.
campagne.firstClearParagraph: The first clear of a stage gives guaranteed rewards (gold, dust, XP, and sometimes a guaranteed piece of equipment or card). Replaying an already-cleared stage gives repeatable rewards, with a chance to drop equipment and cards.
campagne.info: Farm ×3 (sweep) automatically replays an already-cleared stage several times at once, for energy — great for stacking up gold and dust without replaying every battle.

combat-points.intro: Combat points ("energy") are to the campaign what tokens are to pulls. They regenerate passively up to a cap, shown in the topbar.
combat-points.insufficientBullet: Every battle and every farm run uses some. With no energy left, the button reads "Not enough energy".
combat-points.skillsBullet: Some skills speed up their regeneration, raise the cap, and reduce the farm cost.
combat-points.tip: Spend your energy before it hits the cap: beyond that, regenerated points are lost, just like tokens.

cartes.intro: To hold up against advanced stages, your cards need to grow stronger. Three levers combine, all managed from a card's detail sheet.

level.title: Level
level.description: Raise a card's level with gold and dust: its stats (PV, ATQ, DEF, VIT) increase with every level, up to its palier's cap.

ascension.title: Palier & ascension
ascension.description: Once a card is at the top of its <strong1>palier</strong1>, <strong2>ascending it</strong2> consumes a <strong3>duplicate</strong3> to move to the next palier and raise its level cap. Its <strong4>passive</strong4> also grows stronger with each palier, up to a point — beyond that, it stays fixed and only the stats keep improving. Once the max palier is reached, progression continues through <strong5>equipment</strong5>.

equipment.title: Equipment
equipment.description: Every card has 3 slots — Weapon Armor Accessory. Pieces drop in battle (and from bosses), have a rarity, and add stat bonuses. Equip or remove them from the Equipment page.

cartes.tip: After a defeat, two reflexes: rethink your team composition, or level up your cards before heading back to the front.

quetes.intro: Quests give you concrete goals rewarded with tokens, dust, gold, and XP. They progress automatically as you play.
quetes.typesBullet: <strong1>Weekly</strong1> quests reset every Monday; <strong2>One-shot</strong2> quests are done just once.
quetes.claimBullet: A completed quest switches to "Claimed" once you click Claim.
quetes.perfectWeekBullet: Completing every weekly quest unlocks the Perfect Week bonus.

succes.intro: Achievements are long-term goals unlocked by your actions: pulls, leveling up, login streaks, team membership, and many more.
succes.rewardsBullet: Rewards can include cards, tokens, dust, and XP.

chaine.intro: Log in every day to extend your streak. A missed day resets it to zero, but your best streak stays saved.
chaine.milestonesBullet: Streak milestones grant rewards (tokens, dust, gold, XP).
chaine.consistencyBullet: It's the simplest way to build up resources over time: consistency pays off.

recompenses.intro: Many systems drop off rewards to claim: quests, leveling up, login streaks, achievements, and events. They pile up in the notification bell.
recompenses.claimBullet: Claim them one by one, or all at once — quest rewards are claimed separately, from the Quests page.
recompenses.cardBullet: Some contain a card revealed when you claim it.
recompenses.info: Remember to go claim them: the bell's badge shows how many rewards are waiting for you.

classements.intro: Leaderboards show where you stand against other players, across three categories:

collectors.title: Collectors
collectors.description: Ranks by completion rate, distinct cards, and variants.

combat.title: Combat
combat.description: Ranks by the furthest chapter and stage reached in the campaign.
